why: sentence 2 'He did not know the ford' uses perfect wóyde (stative present 'knows') while sentence 8 maps past 'I did not know' to ǵn̥néh₃m̥ and present 'now I know' to wóydh₂e: lexeme woyde gets two English tenses in one record. Use ǵn̥néh₃t (ne ǵn̥néh₃t) in sentence 2.

sentence 6 'The wise one finds a path' uses widét, the same aorist form as 'found' in sentence 1; PIE reads 'found'. Use a present (e.g. a present-stem verb of finding/seeing) or rephrase the English as past.

sentence 5: sodéyet is 3SG but the subject 'the gods' is plural (conjoined clause lacks a subject slot; verb person/number not inherited from the preceding clause's plural subject). Add num PL/subject to the sodeyeti clause; possibly an engine gap in subject inheritance for subjectless kʷe-conjuncts.
